title: In, at, on, to, into: places
goal: Say where you are and where you go without “reach to”
intro: For position: “in” an enclosed space (in the room, in Delhi), “at” a point or event (at the door, at a party), “on” a surface (on the table, on the bus). For movement: “to” a place, “into” inside something. Some verbs don’t take “to” at all: reach, enter, visit, call, attend.

rules.rule: in a room, city, country; at a point, address or event; on a surface, floor, or public transport.
examples: I’m at the station. He’s on the train.

rules.rule: go / come / travel to a place. But: go home, go there, go abroad.
No preposition after reach, enter, visit, attend, call, marry.

mistakes.wrong: We reached to the hotel late.

ex.q: Wait for me ___ the bus stop.
We will reach to Pune by evening.
ex.fixed: We will reach Pune by evening.

ex.q: She is waiting in the train.
ex.fixed: She is waiting on the train.

ex.q: Put the milk back ___ the fridge.

ex.a: I'll call you when I reach the office.

ex.q: Correct this: “I reached to office at nine.”
a: I reached the office at nine
I got to the office at nine
I got to office at nine
ex.y: reach the office, or get to the office.

talk: Describe your journey to work or college: where you start, how you travel (on the bus? in a car?), where you change, and when you reach.
